name: James Cordahi
title: Senior communications trainer and executive coach
bio_short: Communications trainer and executive coach with more than 30 years' experience. Former Bloomberg News and Reuters editor in the Gulf, later corporate affairs leader at Abbott and Mondelez International. Media, corporate communications, crisis and coaching.
bio: James is a communications trainer and executive coach with more than 30 years' experience spanning international journalism, corporate communications and government affairs. He spent 15 years as a foreign correspondent and editor, founding Bloomberg News' business and finance coverage in the Middle East in 2000 and later co-running the Reuters Gulf financial newsroom.  He then moved in-house, leading corporate affairs and communications for Abraaj Capital, government relations for BlackBerry in MENA, and corporate and government affairs for Mondelez International across Eastern Europe, the Middle East and Africa. At Abbott he spent eight years as Senior Director of Government Affairs for the Middle East, Africa and Pakistan, advising executive leadership on reputation, regulatory reform and political risk. A graduate of the University of Cambridge, James holds a Master's degree in Journalism and a Diploma in Economics from the University of London, and is an executive coach trained by the Co-Active Training Institute.  At ISOC, James delivers corporate communications, media training, crisis communication, executive presence, public affairs and executive coaching. He has worked both sides of the interview, as the correspondent asking the questions and as the executive answering to ministers, regulators and the press, which shows participants how their words will be used. James is based in Dubai and trains in English, Arabic and French.

He spent 15 years as a foreign correspondent and editor, reporting on the collapse of the Soviet Union and Yugoslavia for The Economist and the BBC World Service, and serving as senior editor for the Middle East at the Economist Intelligence Unit. He moved to Dubai in 2000 to found Bloomberg News' business and finance coverage, later co-ran the Reuters Gulf financial newsroom, and in 2025 was executive editor of Arabian Gulf Business Insight.  He then moved in-house, leading corporate affairs for Abraaj Capital, where he ran investor communications, media relations and corporate responsibility. He established BlackBerry's government relations function in MENA, then led corporate and government affairs for Mondelez International across Eastern Europe, the Middle East and Africa. At Abbott he spent eight years as Senior Director of Government Affairs for the Middle East, Africa and Pakistan, advising executive leadership on reputation and regulation.  A graduate of the University of Cambridge, James holds a Master's degree in Journalism and a Diploma in Economics from the University of London. He is an executive coach trained by the Co-Active Training Institute and has moderated at forums including the World Economic Forum in Davos.  At ISOC, James delivers corporate communications, media training, crisis communication, executive presence, public affairs and executive coaching. Since 2011 he has trained government spokespeople, ministry teams and multinational brands, and led communications audits for Gulf energy clients. He has worked both sides of the interview, as the correspondent asking the questions and as the executive answering to ministers, regulators and the press, which shows participants how their words will be used. James is based in Dubai and trains in English, Arabic and French.
